title: Spinal Cord Injury
Rehabilitation
hero.text: For patients recovering from spinal cord injury, to support mobility, independence, daily function and long-term adaptation.

overview: A spinal cord injury occurs when damage to the spinal cord disrupts communication between the brain and the body, affecting movement, sensation and essential bodily functions. Depending on the level and severity of the injury, patients may experience changes in mobility, strength, coordination, bladder and bowel control and overall independence.

topics.label: What Is Spinal Cord Injury Rehabilitation?

blocks.text: Spinal cord injury rehabilitation is specialised care for patients whose movement, sensation, coordination or daily function has been affected by damage to the spinal cord.
At Cambridge Hospital, our rehabilitation programme supports recovery following spinal cord injuries caused by trauma, accidents, falls or medical conditions.

Care is delivered by a coordinated, interdisciplinary team working within one structured pathway, combining medical management with physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech and language therapy and cognitive rehabilitation.
Each programme is built around personalised, measurable goals, helping patients improve mobility, rebuild daily living skills, strengthen independence and adapt safely to changes in function.

topics.label: How Spinal Cord Injury Can Affect Patients

blocks.text: Depending on its severity and location, a spinal cord injury may result in paraplegia (loss of movement in the lower body) or quadriplegia (loss of movement across all four limbs), and can affect sensation, strength and daily function.

With rehabilitation, patients may regain movement or other functions affected by the injury. Our whole-person approach supports the medical, emotional and social aspects of recovery as part of one coordinated rehabilitation pathway.

topics.label: Our Spinal Cord Injury Rehabilitation Programme

items: Body-weight supported training is also used to support the goal of regaining the ability to walk, and educational therapy supports recovery and long-term quality of life throughout the programme

blocks.text: Patients typically move to rehabilitation once they are medically stable and ready to participate in a rehabilitation programme. This is an important stage of recovery, when targeted therapy and functional training can support progress towards greater independence.

Because every spinal cord injury is different, our team develops an individualised programme combining physiotherapy, occupational therapy and other specialist therapies according to each patient’s needs.

Patients receive up to 15 hours of structured therapy across a 7-day period, depending on their clinical needs and rehabilitation goals. Families and caregivers are encouraged to take part in appropriate sessions and receive training to support patients at home. A strong support system can also play an important role in helping patients maintain progress after discharge.
